translated_text: Lignières, May 21st - My darling, I saw your telegram this morning in which you ask me for a medical certificate. I'm sending you a copy of the certificate from Dr. Varadé. Explain to the police station that it's dated May 22nd, therefore on July 22nd I'll be in my 7th month of pregnancy, not my 5th. I hope that will be all right. If I have to get a new certificate, which I have to come and which will delay us by at least 48 hours, I'll still get it done and send it to you, but if this is enough, please wait. I'm also sending you a proof of residence certificate that corresponds to the one in Paris. It might be useful. Everything is fine here. The mobilized men are starting to return, and there's more in the village every day. But none will be as happy as yours the day you hold her in your arms—Deep down, I received my little plush toy from you. I'm now so ugly and fat, it's terrible. You won't love me at all anymore. And then there's the great misfortune of Blacky; here, there's no way to be careful, the country dogs are so "fierce" and badly behaved, and Blacky was so provocative, and Kitty is the same—Just at that moment we had so many other worries, it happened near the sad meadow?! My darling, I long so much to see you, to talk to you, it's terribly hard. But now you must be patient a little longer. Perhaps by the end of next week you'll already be at our place. Above all, don't do anything foolish at the last minute. My Bob, I'm waiting for you and adore you. Your little wife, Mr. Robert Zweigenthal, 4th Good 17th Company, Camp d'Agde, Agde. Mrs. Zweigenthal, Lignières (marital).
